The policy extension interface

Source: R/extension.R
policy_interface.Rd

A banditlab policy is an ordinary S3 object with class c("<your_class>", "bandit_policy") and methods for three generics. The experiment engine drives every policy, built-in or user-defined, through this exact lifecycle:

  1. policy_state(policy, arms) is called once per replicate to initialise runtime state. It must return the policy object with any state fields added. Calling it again must produce a fresh state (it is also the reset operation).

  2. select_arm(policy, t) is called at every step t = 1, 2, ... and must return a list with element arm (one of the initialised arm names). Optional elements: propensity, the marginal probability with which the policy selects that arm given its current state (NA if it has no closed form), and reason, a short string.

  3. update_state(policy, arm, reward, t) receives the selected arm and observed reward and must return the updated policy object.

Methods must not set random seeds and must not depend on global mutable state; all randomness must come from the current RNG so that the engine's reproducibility guarantees hold.

One practical note on S3 dispatch: methods defined at the top level of a script or inside a package are found automatically. Methods defined inside other evaluation environments (for example testthat tests or knitr chunks) are invisible to the engine unless registered:

registerS3method("policy_state", "my_policy", policy_state.my_policy)
registerS3method("select_arm", "my_policy", select_arm.my_policy)
registerS3method("update_state", "my_policy", update_state.my_policy)

See vignette("custom-policies", package = "banditlab") for a worked implementation of a softmax policy using only this interface.

Usage

policy_state(policy, arms, ...)

select_arm(policy, t, ...)

update_state(policy, arm, reward, t, ...)

Arguments

policy

A bandit_policy object.

arms

Character vector of arm names supplied by the environment.

...

Reserved for future methods.

t

The current time step, starting at 1.

arm

The selected arm name.

reward

The observed numeric reward.

Value

policy_state() and update_state() return the (initialised or updated) policy object. select_arm() returns a list with elements arm and optionally propensity and reason.

Examples

# A minimal custom policy: always play the first arm.
policy_first <- function() {
  structure(list(), class = c("first_policy", "bandit_policy"))
}
policy_state.first_policy <- function(policy, arms, ...) {
  policy$arms <- arms
  policy
}
select_arm.first_policy <- function(policy, t, ...) {
  list(arm = policy$arms[[1]], propensity = 1, reason = "fixed")
}
update_state.first_policy <- function(policy, arm, reward, t, ...) {
  policy
}
